molarity-calculator.assumptionNote: Assumes the solute dissolves fully in the stated final volume of solution. Volume changes on mixing and incomplete dissolving are not modeled.
benefits: Prepare lab solutions correctly: get the exact grams to weigh for any target molarity.
Convert between mass and moles without looking up formulas each time.
Check homework and exam answers with a trusted reference calculation.
Scale recipes up or down: doubling the volume at the same molarity doubles the mass needed.

faqs.a: Molarity (M) = moles of solute / liters of solution. It tells you how concentrated a solution is. A 1 M solution has 1 mole dissolved in each liter.
Molarity counts moles per liter. Molality counts moles per kilogram of solvent. They are close for dilute water solutions but differ for concentrated ones.
faqs.q: What is the difference between molarity and molality?

faqs.a: Molar mass = the mass of one mole of the substance in g/mol. NaCl is 58.44, glucose (C6H12O6) is 180.16, water is 18.015. Sum the atomic masses of the formula.
faqs.q: How do I find the molar mass?

faqs.a: Rearrange the formula: mass = molarity x volume x molar mass. For 0.5 L of 1 M NaCl: 1 x 0.5 x 58.44 = 29.22 g.
faqs.q: How many grams do I need for a target molarity?

faqs.a: Yes: 1 M = 1000 mM. This calculator shows both units. Biology and medicine often use mM or uM for dilute solutions.
faqs.q: Can I convert between M and mM?

faqs.a: Molarity changes with temperature because liquids expand. If exact work matters, prepare solutions at the lab's working temperature and use volumetric glassware.

molarity-calculator.formula:
Molarity (M) = Moles of solute / Liters of solution

From mass: Moles = Mass (g) / Molar mass (g/mol)
Combined: M = [Mass / Molar mass] / Volume (L)

Example: 58.44 g NaCl (molar mass 58.44 g/mol) in 1 L = (58.44 / 58.44) / 1 = 1.0000 M.
howTo: Choose your input: from mass (enter grams and molar mass) or from moles directly.
Enter the final volume of the solution in liters.
The molarity appears instantly in mol/L (M) and millimolar (mM).
For lab work, weigh out the mass shown and dissolve it in the target volume.
keyFacts: Molarity = moles of solute per liter of solution, written as M or mol/L.
The volume is the final solution volume, not just the water added.
Standard lab solutions are often 0.1 M or 1 M.
Dilution follows M1 x V1 = M2 x V2.
Molarity is temperature-dependent because liquid volumes expand when warm.

molarity-calculator.quickAnswer: Molarity = moles / liters of solution. Dissolving 58.44 g of NaCl (molar mass 58.44 g/mol, so 1 mole) in 1 liter of solution gives exactly 1.0000 M. Enter your mass, molar mass, and volume above for any solution.
molarity-calculator.tagline: Find molar concentration from mass or moles - with results in M and mM.
molarity-calculator.workedExample:
58.44 g NaCl, molar mass 58.44 g/mol, final volume 1 L.
1. Moles = 58.44 / 58.44 = 1.0000 mol.
2. Molarity = 1.0000 / 1 = 1.0000 M.
3. In millimolar: 1.0000 x 1000 = 1000.0000 mM.

Another: 2 moles in 0.5 L = 2 / 0.5 = 4.0000 M.
